sources.title: Chiplets on Wheels: Review Paper on Holistic Chiplet Solutions for Autonomous Vehicles
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The authors position chiplet-based systems as one response to growing automotive high-performance-compute demand alongside centralized E/E architectures.

The paper proposes a throughput-oriented micro-architecture for ADAS and infotainment, a methodology for chiplet evaluation, gem5-based latency/throughput simulation tools, and thermally aware placement/cooling work.
claims.context: Contribution list verified from the primary abstract.

limitations.text: This verification established the contribution set from the primary abstract but did not reconstruct workload definitions, chiplet interconnect assumptions, thermal models, latency/throughput results, or comparative baselines.
The work primarily concerns silicon/chiplet architecture rather than the vehicle-level allocation of I/O, network, software services, and lifecycle responsibilities.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Chiplets on Wheels: Review Paper on Holistic Chiplet Solutions for Autonomous Vehicles; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The primary abstract verifies the proposed chiplet/HPC architecture and simulation/thermal-design scope, but the detailed evaluation setup and quantitative limitations were not reconstructed.

editorial.why_now_note: Chiplet-based HPC may affect future centralized vehicle compute packaging, but it is peripheral to the core E/E architecture transition.
editorial.rationale: Potentially useful silicon/HPC context, but it is below the main vehicle E/E responsibility layer and the full simulation/thermal evaluation was not reconstructed in this pass.
